brief:
The New York Times has gradually adjusted its editorial language on Israel and Gaza since the October 2023 war began, Mondoweiss reported. The shift reflects broader changes in American public sentiment, moving from blanket support for Israel toward more qualified criticism of the conflict.

The newspaper's evolving stance mirrors a wider realignment in US opinion on the Gaza war, though the Times maintains bounds on how far its criticism extends. The paper's incremental changes in framing demonstrate how major outlets adjust positions in response to documented shifts in reader and public viewpoint.
dek: Since the start of the genocide in Gaza, the so-called paper of record has begun to update its language on Israel, reflecting a larger shift in US public opinion.
title: New York Times shifts Gaza coverage as US public opinion moves left
